tier_reason: benchmarks/README.md gives throughput tables against spdlog 1.12.0 sync and async from public code in benchmarks/ (benchmark_main.cpp, fetched spdlog/fmt via benchmarks/CMakeLists.txt), with MSVC 19.44 /O2 /DNDEBUG C++20 and AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX stated; all quoted numbers match the tables.

corrections.caveats: First-party Windows/MSVC benchmark dated 2026-09-22; measures producer-side ops/s, not time to durable disk; spdlog 1.12.0 is not the latest; default 3 runs, so P95/P99 equal the max; Windows clock resolution is 100 ns, so per-call latency figures are coarse; author warns numbers describe one machine and that a run on network storage flatters this library. Also beats spdlog_sync on P99 latency (300 ns vs 32,800 ns) and spdlog_async on thread scaling (9.36M vs 114K ops/s at 16 threads).

notes: Numbers verified against benchmarks/README.md; metadata (MIT, 5 stars, last commit 2026-09-28 Release v2.2.0) matches github.com pages. Very low adoption.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Quill README 1-thread number logging: 6/10 ns at 50th/99.9th vs spdlog 271/360 ns; 4 threads 8/18 ns vs spdlog 557/1106 ns. corrections.caveats: Own README numbers (Ryzen 5950X, g++ 15.3.0, CPU scaling enabled warning) have no spdlog row; the spdlog comparison comes from the Quill author's harness (a competing library's author). Sub-2 ns figures are enqueue-only in a tight loop. Linux and FreeBSD x86-64 only.

notes: Benchmark code for XTR confirmed present in odygrd/logger_benchmarks. MIT, 77 stars, last commit 2026-09-16.

tier_reason: First-party README tables vs tokio-tracing and rustracing across four CPU families and span counts; no compiler/rustc version or flags stated, and gains above 50x with unstated flags cap it at C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: At 100 spans: tokio-tracing 124x slower on Intel Broadwell (33x Skylake, 36x AMD Zen, 29x Graviton2), fastrace 3.4 us on Broadwell; by span count tokio-tracing is 19x slower at 1 span (fastrace 0.4 us) up to 151x at 1000 spans (fastrace 27.8 us). rustracing 9x to 55x slower.
corrections.caveats: Baseline is tokio-tracing (and rustracing), not the OpenTelemetry SDK; first-party numbers; CPU families named but not exact models; rustc version and flags not stated; benches/results not opened; successor of tikv/minitrace-rust (not a GitHub fork). Rust library, not C++.

notes: README numbers match. Apache-2.0, 1.1k stars, last commit 2026-07-31.
